description: Law No. 296 of 2001, revising Legislative Decree No. 11614 of 1969, prohibits 'any person who is not a national of a recognized state' from acquiring real estate of any kind. It does not mention Palestinians and applies to almost nobody else.
energy_note: A law about statelessness, aimed at one people.

description: Palestinians had held property rights in Lebanon for decades before 2001. This was a removal, not a continuation.
energy_note: A right they had, taken back.

description: Parliamentarians petitioned the Constitutional Council to review the clause as a breach of constitutional bans on discrimination. The petition failed and the Council affirmed the clause.

aspect: No property means no inheritance and no collateral
description: Three generations of work cannot be converted into an asset, passed to a child, or borrowed against to start anything. The family's savings have nowhere to become capital.
money_note: Value of a lifetime's housing equity never accrued.
energy_note: Seventy years of rent and nothing to leave anyone.

aspect: The stated purpose is to prevent settlement
description: The aim is widely acknowledged to be preventing permanent settlement of Palestinians in Lebanon. The instrument for preventing permanence is to make seventy years of residence produce nothing.
energy_note: Kept temporary, on purpose, for three generations.
